Part A, the relevance contract: (1) the signals and how they combine: from the props type itself (explicit own members always; keys of `Pick<X,'a'|'b'>` named on purpose, `Omit` says nothing about the rest; members that override/narrow a base member; JSDoc, `@default`, literal-union and required members); spreads (a `{...rest}` on a DOM tag = the ambient DOM attributes, ignore; a spread onto a COMPONENT = one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, resolve the JSX tag by symbol/import; attributes set AFTER the spread are fixed and subtracted, attributes set BEFORE it are overridable defaults and kept, an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing); call-site evidence (the props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project and in stories' `args`, with a frequency floor of 20%, as measured in relevance-baseline.md: about 0.3 to 0.8 extra rows per component); `handed_on` = unknown, never guessed. (2) The OUTPUT: what changes in the JSON (propose: a short `used` list on a collapsed layer instead of full rows for universal props like className/style/id; whether a per-prop flag is needed), the consumers' rules (Storybook argTypes selection and its option to expand; agent output deferred), the schema/version/changeset implications, and the acceptance gate: T5's coverage metric (shrink/relevance/ scripts) must rise while rows shown fall; give targets from the baseline (e.g. shadcn coverage 0.43 mean today). Part B, the checker scheduler (the owner asked for a queue): items are 'the props we will show' of a component, not whole components; priority classes (on-screen > neighbouring stories > background fill) with preemption and cancel on edit/navigation; batching by snapshot so queued components share the program and the converter memo; admission control on a memory budget read from the allocator (the arena guard only reads the checker's arenas; see shrink/chakra-memory.md); stream each result when ready; map every piece onto what exists today with file:line (the addon's prefetch queue in background.ts, `Completions`, the lifecycle reducer, OnDemand lanes, the CLI's one-shot batch, the heap-budget slice B in flight) and say what is NEW. Be explicit about what you could not determine. Part C, a slice plan with DISJOINT files so tracks can run in parallel and merge in order: T2 (props-type signals in the resolver), T3 (forwarding resolution: depends on PR 470), T4 (consumers: addon argTypes selection, docs, weekly row), the scheduler slices, and the factory-wrapper own-props slice (the census found `chakra("div",{variants})` and Spectrum `createLeafComponent`/`createBranchComponent` hide own props), each with its gate, the files it owns, its dependencies, an estimate of lines, and the first test that must fail on main. Keep it under about 4 pages; bullets, no tables (the Entire trail view does not render tables, ADRs may use them sparingly). Run the repo's doc checks (`just doc-check`, `just lint` parts that touch docs/markdown: oxfmt on the md, typos). Self-review: run `/code-review medium` on your commit and fix real findings in one round. Do NOT push: commit locally, report the SHA. PR body to /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/docs-adr-0028-relevance-and-scheduler.md (`## What`, `## Not verified`, session URL line from your system reminder). Cap 60 tool calls. # Worker contract (caliper). Read once; the brief only names the task, the files you own and the call cap.

Scope
- Edit only the files the brief names. If another file must change, stop and say which and why.
- Never ask the user questions. If blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work: finish or report.

Branch and push
- Branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/<task>/. Scratch there too, never /tmp.
- Rust 1.99.1 on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin) for builds; commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 (the mise shim forces 1.98.1). Caveat: with the toolchain bin first on PATH `rust-objcopy` can fail and strip silently does nothing; irrelevant unless you measure binary size.
- Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:<branch>`), never --no-verify, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Do not open or edit the PR, do not poll CI.

Checks: targeted, CI runs the rest
- Always, before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos` (fast).
- Then only what your change touches: Rust -> nextest of the touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once; checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` vs a build of origin/main on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src (tools: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/same.py, identity.sh; ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/final-perf/ab.sh interleaves two binaries).
- Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless you changed those areas: CI runs them on every PR.
- Tests that fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one.
- No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, and prefer allocation or instruction counts (load-independent).

Cap
- Stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what you have verified. Listing something as 'not done' with its cause beats burning more calls.

Artifacts (agents to agents; humans see them at the edge)
- Write the PR body to ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<branch, slashes as dashes>.md: `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line `https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. The lead publishes it unedited.
- Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers. Nothing else.

Its precedence rule and its default moved to `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` and `docs/performance.md`.
- 11. Find dependency declarations through a per-package export index, not the parse cache — removed: how one module stores what it loaded. It lives in `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` ("Persisted export index").
- 12. Collapse large inherited dependency sources, as Storybook does — removed: a default and a threshold one module reads. It lives in `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` ("Collapse"), where the rule is now relevance (ambient and large), not size alone: a dependency's own API is listed (a non-ambient source collapses past 200 props).
- 13. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own — removed: a resolver behavior of an opt-in mode. It lives in `docs/rdt-coverage.md` ("Curated reads React apart").
- 14. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut — removed: a lookup order. It lives in `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` ("Precedence").
- 15. A member read through React's types reads React's declaration and what it imports — removed: a resolver behavior, not a structure. It lives in `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md` ("Member reads through React's types").
- [16. Extends 0010's loading from "before resolution" to "before the resolution that answers".
- [17. Version the canonical JSON, and make readers reject a version they don't read](0017-version-the-canonical-json.md) — do not change the canonical JSON's shape without bumping `SCHEMA_VERSION`, or let a reader accept a version it was not written for.
- [18. Extends 0009's per-prop table to the lists that repeat across components; `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2.
- 19. Load dependency declarations by default — removed: a default, with its measurements. It lives in `docs/performance.md` ("Default changes").
- 20. Chain dependency layers and load the remaining names after three growths — removed: a tuning of 0016's design with measurements, not a new decision. It lives in `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md` ("Demand-driven dependencies") and `docs/performance.md`. It replaced 0016's 48-growth threshold.
- 21. Publish the semantic backend crates with the CLI — removed: a release procedure. Callisto publishes `caliper-docgen-semantic` before the CLI (`callisto.toml`, `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`); 0007's always-compiled backend is why it is a public crate.
- [22. Ask a warm checker for the requested component](0022-ask-a-warm-checker-for-the-requested-component.md) — do not route by predicted risk or check the whole project to answer one story: ask the TypeScript checker for the component a request names, wait a bounded time, and take the structural answer when it is slower. Extends 0007's runtime opt-in from a project run to a session.
- 23. Function parameters carry `optional` and `rest` — removed: a field added under 0017's versioning rule. It lives in `docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md` ("Version 3").
- 24. List every HTML attribute React declares by default — removed: a default, with its measurements. It lives in `docs/rdt-coverage.md` ("Why `full` is the default") and `docs/performance.md` ("Default changes").
- [25. The resolver owns scoping; the extractor records where a declaration sits](0025-resolver-owns-scoping.md) — do not decide in a collector which declaration a name refers to, or re-derive an import's type-only status: the extractor records each declaration with its enclosing scope, the resolver looks names up by scope, and `is_type_only` is read from the import.
- [26. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax](0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md) — Accepted. Do not make a type decision in a projection, key a cache on a checker type id, or bump the pinned tsrs without the construct suite and a parity run against the Go checker: the checker gives the prop set, types, requiredness and descriptions, oxc the candidates, defaults, positions and declaration order, and the structural resolver is only the fallback. Supersedes in part 0006 and 0007.
- [27. Identify a component by its declaration and its exports, not its display name](0027-identify-a-component-by-its-declaration-and-exports.md) — Accepted. Do not pair, dedupe or cache a component by its display name, fall back to a module's `default` export, or re-derive a component's exports outside the extractor: the extractor records each component's exports, the checker is asked for that export by name, its answers pair by output key, dedupe is by declaration, and the canonical JSON carries `exports` for readers to join on.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR. A removed entry keeps its number; its rationale moved to the doc named on its line.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A default, threshold or resolution order that one module reads (a collapse limit, a growth count, which lookup goes first) — that's a code comment plus the subsystem's `docs/architecture/` page. Measurements belong in `docs/performance.md`.
- A release or CI procedure (what to publish first, which gate blocks) — that's the workflow file.
- A field added to the canonical JSON under 0017's versioning rule — the `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and `docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md` record it. Write one only when the contract's structure changes, as 0018 did.
- A default flipped after a measurement — the numbers go in `docs/performance.md` and the new default in the option's doc comment.
- A superseded or tuned earlier decision whose design still holds — update the architecture page, don't stack a new ADR on it. Write one only if the contract itself changes.
- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.
# 0026. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax

**Status:** Accepted (2026-11-08) **Date:** 2026-11-07

## Context

ADR 0006 and 0007 made the TypeScript checker an opt-in second resolver, because a whole-project `tsc` run cost up to 9.3 s and 975 MiB (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`); ADR 0022 bounded it to a warm per-component request. The structural default still answers wrong without a marker: a type that is only a call signature becomes `{}`, `Omit`, `Pick` and `Partial` reached through an alias lose their effect, and a factory's props are taken from a name-matched interface (`docs/rdt-differences.md`, classes 4 to 6). A prototype found more: `[string, ...number[]]` prints as `[string, number[][]]` and a getter reads as a method. Each fix is another rule in a resolver that re-implements the type system.

tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. A throwaway prototype through the Node client (not in the repository; these numbers are the record) measured on Chakra `ButtonProps` (1,138 props) a 43-47 ms snapshot and the first converted prop at 62-67 ms, where ADR 0022 measured 703 ms with `tsc` on a different program root (indicative, not an A/B), with tsrs peaking at 126-130 MiB. On 16 hand-written components the checker was equal or better on 14, worse on union member order and an unresolvable import. A polymorphic component instantiated through a virtual file gave 267 props for `'div'` where both engines give 2 today. tsrs's own benchmark (`bench/RESULTS.md`) reports 1.8 to 4.2 times TypeScript 7.1 beta's speed and 2.1 to 2.6 times less memory.

## Decision

The checker decides types and oxc decides syntax.

- **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.
- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` (`checker: false` in the config, the napi binding and the Storybook addon) turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` are removed (S8).
- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint was re-measured with tsrs in S4 and holds (Chakra's `Button`, 562 ms, 402 ms after the first-answer work). The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).
- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose, never through dependabot (its ignore list); the npm `tsrs` the parity gate runs (`apps/oracle`, `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) moves with them, and `scripts/check-packaging.mjs` fails while the two name different releases. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.
- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed, and there is no other checker to choose. The Go `typescript` beta is the oracle, the construct goldens and the parity gate, in `apps/oracle` only. The linked checker is never replaced, since a fresh session raises this process's memory rather than returning it; past `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, read from its own arenas, it stops for the session and components keep their structural answer with a diagnostic. A panic closes its session and a fresh one answers the next request, and a file nested past 20,000 brackets is not given to it (trail 369 slice 2).
- **React element types.** The checker keeps `ReactElement` and `JSX.Element` as `named` types with their arguments, found by their declaration in `@types/react` (`JSX.Element` named through its namespace, apart from the DOM's `Element`); only `ReactNode` is the `reactNode` terminal. Amended 2026-11-13: this bullet first kept them collapsed to `reactNode`, which is wider (it also admits strings, numbers and `null`) and carried no `degradedBy`, so the construct suite's checker lane scored `react/03` to `05` less precise. The structural fallback still collapses them. No schema change: `named` already holds them.

Linked rather than spawned (trail 369): the crates are published (0.24.0), the same recorded Chakra answer (3,776 requests) takes 141 ms in process against 367 ms over the pipe with equal answers, and there is no per-platform binary to ship or find. What it costs: a stack overflow inside the checker aborts the host process (the 512 MiB thread holds a type 10,000 deep and tsrs's 256 MiB parse threads one 200,000 deep; past 20,000 brackets a file is refused, but nesting written without brackets, such as a chain of 700,000 arrow types, is not bounded), a dropped session does not return its memory (trail 369 slice 2, done: it bounds the checker's arenas and then answers structurally, [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#in-process-guards-trail-369-slice-2)), and each linked artifact grows by about 22 MB.

Trail 369 slice 4 (done, 2026-11-12) deleted the product's process route: `--tsc-path` and `tscPath` (CLI, config, napi, Storybook addon), `crates/tsc-client`, the binary lookup and the version allow-list it checked, and the replay tests that ran recordings of the Go checker through a fake `tsc` process; those tests ask the linked checker now. Slice 5's pin rule is in **Pin** above. Spawning a binary stays rejected (Alternatives).

## Consequences

- Supersedes "structural stays the default" in ADR 0006 and 0007 and 0007's "never a silent default" trigger. The rest of both stands.
- Deletable or shrinkable with a thin fallback, estimated from each file's header: in `crates/core/src/resolver`, `alias`, `chain`, `evaluate`, `substitute`, `named`, `primitives`, `extends`, `func`, `template`, `import`, `callee`, `memo`, `deps`, `collected` and `precedence` shrink to a no-generics subset and `mod.rs` by half; `dependency_types.rs` and `import_map.rs` go (the checker resolves modules; ADR 0010 and 0025 narrow to the fallback); in `extractor`, `interface` (but cva), `alias`, `values`, `reexports`, `asserted` and most of `visit` go, and `component`, `wrapper` and `mod.rs` shrink to candidate detection. About 7,600 of 25,300 non-test lines, 9,400 with no fallback, which Windows ARM64 rules out. `html`, `react`, `ambient`, `evidence`, `uses`, `defaults` and `jsdoc` stay; `crates/semantic` grows and `convert.rs` is rewritten (`crates/tsc-client`, the process route's client, is gone since trail 369 slice 4).
- Contract: `PropType` gains what the checker knows and it cannot hold: tuple element optional, rest and labels, `bigint`, `unique symbol`, enum identity, template literals, overload sets, call signatures on objects, a recursion marker, and a typed truncation in place of `Named` with checker text. React terminals (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `Ref`, `ElementType`, HTML attributes) are recognized by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` (`crates/semantic/src/component.rs`) does. `SCHEMA_VERSION` and `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (ADR 0017).
- No cache is keyed on a type id: ids are per checker and change with query order. Keys are file content, export name, instantiation and the tsrs pin. The checker does not see an edit it is not told about, so watch forwards every change. The whole-project `extract` keeps its answer on disk for the whole program only, keyed by every question its linked checker asked of the file system (failed lookups included) with a digest of each answer, the build's fingerprint (the pin with it) and the request; any different answer discards it whole (2026-11-12, `docs/type-checker-integration.md`).
- Unsolved: a per-component dependency closure from the checker (invalidation stays conservative), and the structural answer's gaps wherever the fallback runs.
- Risks: tsrs is pre-1.0, four releases in twelve days, and closed to pull requests (its README). Memory grew from 98 to 246 MB over 150 Chakra edits with each old snapshot disposed (#920 and #646 open). Determinism across checker counts is shown only on a 72-file program. There is no `@tsrs/win32-arm64` package, so those users get the fallback. The linked crates add about 22 MB to the CLI and to the napi binding.

Migration, each slice behind a deterministic gate, none on the oracle. The tsrs backend (the Rust client running on tsrs, PR 390) is done.

1. **S1** (done) Shared projection model and the new `PropType` variants, filled by the structural path where it knows them. Gate: a unit test per variant, golden JSON diff, cache schema test.
2. **S2** (done) Flag-based converter in `convert.rs`, memoized by type id within one snapshot, with a named-boundary policy and caps. Gate: the construct suite's expected JSON; reversed query order gives identical bytes.
3. **S3** (done) React terminals by declaring path. Gate: no regression against today's Chakra `Button` terminals.
4. **S4** (done, one gate failed) The checker's answer wins when it runs: the addon inside ADR 0022's window, the CLI waiting (`--semantic-timeout-ms`, 10 s), and a prop the checker could not read keeps its structural type with `degradedBy` (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`). Gate: checker-on output equals structural on the suite except a listed set of improvements (held by the checker lane); Chakra first answer at most 150 ms through the Rust client (measured 562 ms, then 402 ms once each answer was parsed once and a type's parts asked for once; FAIL: the floor of that request set with no round trips is about 230 ms, 81% of its bytes the property lists of Chakra's style-prop condition maps, so the seam has to change rather than the budget: [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#first-answer-s4), and ADR 0022's structural-first answer stands); the Storybook harness re-run (not run: it needs the corpora).
5. **S5** (done) Instantiation of generic and polymorphic components through a virtual file: a component whose first type parameter declares a default is read at it, from a file the checker holds in memory (`createSnapshot`'s `fileSystem` layer, read by tsrs and the Go beta alike) in a second snapshot made only when a requested component is generic; an instantiation that does not form keeps the structural props with the checker's error as the reason ([generic components](../type-checker-integration.md#generic-components-adr-0026-slice-s5)). Gate: `Poly<'div'>` gives at least 260 props and `'a'` differs (PASS: 281 and 289, on tsrs and the Go checker, `crates/semantic/tests/instantiate.rs`).
6. **S6** (done, one gate failed) Watch on `snapshot.update` with RSS recycling: the warm checker keeps its snapshot and brings it up to date with `updateSnapshot` (`ensurePrograms`, the files the session announced), and before an answer compares every file its program read with the stamp it had; an unannounced change answers from a fresh snapshot with a warning naming the file ([watch](../type-checker-integration.md#watch-adr-0026-slice-s6)). Gate: an unnotified edit fails a test loudly (PASS, `crates/semantic/tests/watch.rs`, on tsrs and the Go checker); Chakra edit-and-query p95 at most 25 ms (PASS at 22.6 ms for a component with props of its own in the Chakra program; FAIL at 565 ms and more for one of Chakra's `ButtonProps`, whose floor is converting its 1,140 props, 330 ms on an unchanged snapshot, while the checker's CPU per edit fell from 437 to 737 ms to 56 to 70: [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#watch-on-snapshotupdate-s6)); 300 Chakra edits stay under the threshold (PASS, peak 321 to 357 MiB against 768, 5 `worn` replacements, answers byte-identical to a fresh session's).
7. **S7** Delete the structural resolver for what the suite covers. Gate: every suite row passes with the fallback off on supported platforms; a Windows ARM64 job runs the fallback. (Windows was dropped as a supported platform afterwards, trail 370, so that job no longer exists.) Before any of it goes, the facts the merge took from it come from elsewhere: **S7a** (done) the checker supplies `parent`, `declarations`, tags and `composes` (gate-large: 467,019 of the 467,221 props only the checker returns carry `parent`; the other 202 are members of type literals, which have no parent by definition); **S7a2** (done) oxc's syntax supplies `defaultValue` and union member order, and the checker lane passes with the resolver's answer for them off (`--no-resolver-facts`; [defaults and union order](../type-checker-integration.md#defaults-and-union-order-adr-0026-slice-s7a2)); **S7b** (gate measured) a hidden, test-only `extract --no-structural-fallback` (`ResolverFacts::NoFallback`) merges with no structural fallback, and the checker lane runs every row with it, holding the rows that change in `checker-expectations.json` (`"fallback"`, by cause): 5 of 252, 4 `structural description` (`cross-file/02`, `objects/38`, `objects/39`, `utility-mapped/36`: the checker returns no description the golden has) and 1 `checker could not read: indexedAccess` (`generics/29`), the worklist of S7c to S7e. Fourteen rows (`components`, `cross-file`) cover what only the structural path's own tests held: components made by calls, a `default`-keyed export list, lib-typed functions, a hook's return type, imports, re-exports and shadowed names; all 14 pass on the checker. **S7c** (gate on) the 4 description rows were a missing request: the checker is not asked for a description the structural pass already has (`SemanticTarget::described`, 65% of Mantine's requests), and with no fallback nothing took its place; `ResolverFacts::ready` asks for every description under `NoFallback`, so the default `extract` is unchanged. `generics/29` is a genuine limit: `T["name"]` is an indexed access the checker defers while `T` is open, and PropType has no shape for it, so its answer is the typed `opaque` (`indexedAccess`) with `degradedBy` and a warning. The lane now fails any row that leans on the fallback, listed or not, except a `checker could not read: <kinds>` entry that says in `"limit"` why it is one.
8. **S8** (done, 2026-11-12) Make the checker the default (`--no-checker`, `checker: false`), and the docs. The owner flipped it on every surface, `extract` included, knowing the structural speed lead no longer describes the default: `extract` of `gate-large` takes 6.0 s and 970 MiB with the checker against 0.10 s and 200 MiB with `--no-checker` ([gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#the-checker-is-the-default-s8)). The Vite plugin, which has no switch and serves whole outputs, and `watch` stay structural. A session's kept checker answers now share their props, which a session asking every story would otherwise have held at about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component. Gate: `just lint doc-check machete typos` (PASS), and the list below.

### Gates before the default flips

- The checker lane of the construct suite (caliper's checker path over `apps/oracle/construct-suite`) shows no regression against the structural path except listed improvements. **PASS**: `just test-checker-lane` on the S8 branch.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/skills/adr

**Goal:** A future contributor (or you, in six months) understands why a hard-to-reverse architectural decision was made, in under a minute of reading.

## Decide if it's ADR material

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural** — it affects system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format/contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code** — if it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, skip it — it's a commit message, a code comment, or a line in `rdt-coverage.md`, not an ADR. A clever algorithm confined to one function, a naming convention, a behavior-preserving refactor: none of these are architectural even if someone spent real thought on them.

Unsure? Ask rather than guess — writing one nobody wanted is worse than skipping one that mattered.

## Write it

Full rules and voice guide: `docs/adr/README.md`. Template: `docs/adr/0000-template.md`. Read both before writing — don't rely on memory of them.

Find the next number by listing `docs/adr/*.md` and incrementing the highest. Copy the template, but treat its sections as a starting shape, not a form to fill mechanically — a one-paragraph decision doesn't need a forced "Alternatives considered" with nothing real in it. Cut sections that would just say "n/a."

Ground every claim in something checkable — a file, a line, a number, a test you actually ran. If you're about to write "this is faster" or "this was necessary," go verify it first (read the code, run the test, check git history) instead of asserting from a vague sense that it's probably true.

Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column. One line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap — matches every other doc in this repo.

## Before you save it

Read it back once as the target contributor, not the author. Cut every sentence that would survive being deleted — check against `docs/adr/README.md`'s banned-word list and before/after table. If a section reads like a corporate template ("In conclusion, this represents..."), delete it; ADRs stop when the decision's been explained, they don't wrap up with a summary of themselves.

Short beats complete. If the technical depth genuinely doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see how `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` points at `docs/type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

30	- 21. Publish the semantic backend crates with the CLI — removed: a release procedure. Callisto publishes `caliper-docgen-semantic` before the CLI (`callisto.toml`, `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`); 0007's always-compiled backend is why it is a public crate.
31	- [22. Ask a warm checker for the requested component](0022-ask-a-warm-checker-for-the-requested-component.md) — do not route by predicted risk or check the whole project to answer one story: ask the TypeScript checker for the component a request names, wait a bounded time, and take the structural answer when it is slower. Extends 0007's runtime opt-in from a project run to a session.
32	- 23. Function parameters carry `optional` and `rest` — removed: a field added under 0017's versioning rule. It lives in `docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md` ("Version 3").
33	- 24. List every HTML attribute React declares by default — removed: a default, with its measurements. It lives in `docs/rdt-coverage.md` ("Why `full` is the default") and `docs/performance.md` ("Default changes").
34	- [25. The resolver owns scoping; the extractor records where a declaration sits](0025-resolver-owns-scoping.md) — do not decide in a collector which declaration a name refers to, or re-derive an import's type-only status: the extractor records each declaration with its enclosing scope, the resolver looks names up by scope, and `is_type_only` is read from the import.
35	- [26. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax](0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md) — Accepted. Do not make a type decision in a projection, key a cache on a checker type id, or bump the pinned tsrs without the construct suite and a parity run against the Go checker: the checker gives the prop set, types, requiredness and descriptions, oxc the candidates, defaults, positions and declaration order, and the structural resolver is only the fallback. Supersedes in part 0006 and 0007.
36	- [27. Identify a component by its declaration and its exports, not its display name](0027-identify-a-component-by-its-declaration-and-exports.md) — Accepted. Do not pair, dedupe or cache a component by its display name, fall back to a module's `default` export, or re-derive a component's exports outside the extractor: the extractor records each component's exports, the checker is asked for that export by name, its answers pair by output key, dedupe is by declaration, and the canonical JSON carries `exports` for readers to join on.
37	
38	Changing any of these needs a new ADR. A removed entry keeps its number; its rationale moved to the doc named on its line.
39	
40	## When to write one
41	
42	Two gates, both required:
43	
44	1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
45	2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?
46	
47	If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.
48	
49	Good candidates:
50	
51	- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
52	- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
53	- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned
54	
55	Not ADR material:
56	
57	- A default, threshold or resolution order that one module reads (a collapse limit, a growth count, which lookup goes first) — that's a code comment plus the subsystem's `docs/architecture/` page. Measurements belong in `docs/performance.md`.
58	- A release or CI procedure (what to publish first, which gate blocks) — that's the workflow file.
59	- A field added to the canonical JSON under 0017's versioning rule — the `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and `docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md` record it. Write one only when the contract's structure changes, as 0018 did.
60	- A default flipped after a measurement — the numbers go in `docs/performance.md` and the new default in the option's doc comment.
61	- A superseded or tuned earlier decision whose design still holds — update the architecture page, don't stack a new ADR on it. Write one only if the contract itself changes.
62	- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
63	- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
64	- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
65	- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
66	- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
67	- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory
68	
69	## Format
70	
71	One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.
72	
73	- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
74	- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
75	- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.
76	
77	## Writing it
78	
79	Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.
80	
81	**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.
82	
83	| Instead of | Write |
84	| --- | --- |
85	| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
86	| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
87	| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
88	| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |
89	
90	**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.
91	
92	**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.
93	
94	**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.
95	
96	**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.
97	
98	**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.
99	
100	## What good looks like
101	
102	Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.
103	# 0026. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax
104	
105	**Status:** Accepted (2026-11-08) **Date:** 2026-11-07
106	
107	## Context
108	
109	ADR 0006 and 0007 made the TypeScript checker an opt-in second resolver, because a whole-project `tsc` run cost up to 9.3 s and 975 MiB (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`); ADR 0022 bounded it to a warm per-component request. The structural default still answers wrong without a marker: a type that is only a call signature becomes `{}`, `Omit`, `Pick` and `Partial` reached through an alias lose their effect, and a factory's props are taken from a name-matched interface (`docs/rdt-differences.md`, classes 4 to 6). A prototype found more: `[string, ...number[]]` prints as `[string, number[][]]` and a getter reads as a method. Each fix is another rule in a resolver that re-implements the type system.
110	
111	tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. A throwaway prototype through the Node client (not in the repository; these numbers are the record) measured on Chakra `ButtonProps` (1,138 props) a 43-47 ms snapshot and the first converted prop at 62-67 ms, where ADR 0022 measured 703 ms with `tsc` on a different program root (indicative, not an A/B), with tsrs peaking at 126-130 MiB. On 16 hand-written components the checker was equal or better on 14, worse on union member order and an unresolvable import. A polymorphic component instantiated through a virtual file gave 267 props for `'div'` where both engines give 2 today. tsrs's own benchmark (`bench/RESULTS.md`) reports 1.8 to 4.2 times TypeScript 7.1 beta's speed and 2.1 to 2.6 times less memory.
112	
113	## Decision
114	
115	The checker decides types and oxc decides syntax.
116	
117	- **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
118	- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.
119	- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
120	- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` (`checker: false` in the config, the napi binding and the Storybook addon) turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` are removed (S8).
121	- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint was re-measured with tsrs in S4 and holds (Chakra's `Button`, 562 ms, 402 ms after the first-answer work). The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).
122	- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose, never through dependabot (its ignore list); the npm `tsrs` the parity gate runs (`apps/oracle`, `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) moves with them, and `scripts/check-packaging.mjs` fails while the two name different releases. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.
123	- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed, and there is no other checker to choose. The Go `typescript` beta is the oracle, the construct goldens and the parity gate, in `apps/oracle` only. The linked checker is never replaced, since a fresh session raises this process's memory rather than returning it; past `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, read from its own arenas, it stops for the session and components keep their structural answer with a diagnostic. A panic closes its session and a fresh one answers the next request, and a file nested past 20,000 brackets is not given to it (trail 369 slice 2).
124	- **React element types.** The checker keeps `ReactElement` and `JSX.Element` as `named` types with their arguments, found by their declaration in `@types/react` (`JSX.Element` named through its namespace, apart from the DOM's `Element`); only `ReactNode` is the `reactNode` terminal. Amended 2026-11-13: this bullet first kept them collapsed to `reactNode`, which is wider (it also admits strings, numbers and `null`) and carried no `degradedBy`, so the construct suite's checker lane scored `react/03` to `05` less precise. The structural fallback still collapses them. No schema change: `named` already holds them.
125	
126	Linked rather than spawned (trail 369): the crates are published (0.24.0), the same recorded Chakra answer (3,776 requests) takes 141 ms in process against 367 ms over the pipe with equal answers, and there is no per-platform binary to ship or find. What it costs: a stack overflow inside the checker aborts the host process (the 512 MiB thread holds a type 10,000 deep and tsrs's 256 MiB parse threads one 200,000 deep; past 20,000 brackets a file is refused, but nesting written without brackets, such as a chain of 700,000 arrow types, is not bounded), a dropped session does not return its memory (trail 369 slice 2, done: it bounds the checker's arenas and then answers structurally, [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#in-process-guards-trail-369-slice-2)), and each linked artifact grows by about 22 MB.
127	
128	Trail 369 slice 4 (done, 2026-11-12) deleted the product's process route: `--tsc-path` and `tscPath` (CLI, config, napi, Storybook addon), `crates/tsc-client`, the binary lookup and the version allow-list it checked, and the replay tests that ran recordings of the Go checker through a fake `tsc` process; those tests ask the linked checker now. Slice 5's pin rule is in **Pin** above. Spawning a binary stays rejected (Alternatives).
129	
130	## Consequences
131	
132	- Supersedes "structural stays the default" in ADR 0006 and 0007 and 0007's "never a silent default" trigger. The rest of both stands.
133	- Deletable or shrinkable with a thin fallback, estimated from each file's header: in `crates/core/src/resolver`, `alias`, `chain`, `evaluate`, `substitute`, `named`, `primitives`, `extends`, `func`, `template`, `import`, `callee`, `memo`, `deps`, `collected` and `precedence` shrink to a no-generics subset and `mod.rs` by half; `dependency_types.rs` and `import_map.rs` go (the checker resolves modules; ADR 0010 and 0025 narrow to the fallback); in `extractor`, `interface` (but cva), `alias`, `values`, `reexports`, `asserted` and most of `visit` go, and `component`, `wrapper` and `mod.rs` shrink to candidate detection. About 7,600 of 25,300 non-test lines, 9,400 with no fallback, which Windows ARM64 rules out. `html`, `react`, `ambient`, `evidence`, `uses`, `defaults` and `jsdoc` stay; `crates/semantic` grows and `convert.rs` is rewritten (`crates/tsc-client`, the process route's client, is gone since trail 369 slice 4).
134	- Contract: `PropType` gains what the checker knows and it cannot hold: tuple element optional, rest and labels, `bigint`, `unique symbol`, enum identity, template literals, overload sets, call signatures on objects, a recursion marker, and a typed truncation in place of `Named` with checker text. React terminals (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `Ref`, `ElementType`, HTML attributes) are recognized by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` (`crates/semantic/src/component.rs`) does. `SCHEMA_VERSION` and `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (ADR 0017).
135	- No cache is keyed on a type id: ids are per checker and change with query order. Keys are file content, export name, instantiation and the tsrs pin. The checker does not see an edit it is not told about, so watch forwards every change. The whole-project `extract` keeps its answer on disk for the whole program only, keyed by every question its linked checker asked of the file system (failed lookups included) with a digest of each answer, the build's fingerprint (the pin with it) and the request; any different answer discards it whole (2026-11-12, `docs/type-checker-integration.md`).
136	- Unsolved: a per-component dependency closure from the checker (invalidation stays conservative), and the structural answer's gaps wherever the fallback runs.
137	- Risks: tsrs is pre-1.0, four releases in twelve days, and closed to pull requests (its README). Memory grew from 98 to 246 MB over 150 Chakra edits with each old snapshot disposed (#920 and #646 open). Determinism across checker counts is shown only on a 72-file program. There is no `@tsrs/win32-arm64` package, so those users get the fallback. The linked crates add about 22 MB to the CLI and to the napi binding.
138	
139	Migration, each slice behind a deterministic gate, none on the oracle. The tsrs backend (the Rust client running on tsrs, PR 390) is done.
140	
141	1. **S1** (done) Shared projection model and the new `PropType` variants, filled by the structural path where it knows them. Gate: a unit test per variant, golden JSON diff, cache schema test.
142	2. **S2** (done) Flag-based converter in `convert.rs`, memoized by type id within one snapshot, with a named-boundary policy and caps. Gate: the construct suite's expected JSON; reversed query order gives identical bytes.
143	3. **S3** (done) React terminals by declaring path. Gate: no regression against today's Chakra `Button` terminals.
144	4. **S4** (done, one gate failed) The checker's answer wins when it runs: the addon inside ADR 0022's window, the CLI waiting (`--semantic-timeout-ms`, 10 s), and a prop the checker could not read keeps its structural type with `degradedBy` (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`). Gate: checker-on output equals structural on the suite except a listed set of improvements (held by the checker lane); Chakra first answer at most 150 ms through the Rust client (measured 562 ms, then 402 ms once each answer was parsed once and a type's parts asked for once; FAIL: the floor of that request set with no round trips is about 230 ms, 81% of its bytes the property lists of Chakra's style-prop condition maps, so the seam has to change rather than the budget: [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#first-answer-s4), and ADR 0022's structural-first answer stands); the Storybook harness re-run (not run: it needs the corpora).
145	5. **S5** (done) Instantiation of generic and polymorphic components through a virtual file: a component whose first type parameter declares a default is read at it, from a file the checker holds in memory (`createSnapshot`'s `fileSystem` layer, read by tsrs and the Go beta alike) in a second snapshot made only when a requested component is generic; an instantiation that does not form keeps the structural props with the checker's error as the reason ([generic components](../type-checker-integration.md#generic-components-adr-0026-slice-s5)). Gate: `Poly<'div'>` gives at least 260 props and `'a'` differs (PASS: 281 and 289, on tsrs and the Go checker, `crates/semantic/tests/instantiate.rs`).
146	6. **S6** (done, one gate failed) Watch on `snapshot.update` with RSS recycling: the warm checker keeps its snapshot and brings it up to date with `updateSnapshot` (`ensurePrograms`, the files the session announced), and before an answer compares every file its program read with the stamp it had; an unannounced change answers from a fresh snapshot with a warning naming the file ([watch](../type-checker-integration.md#watch-adr-0026-slice-s6)). Gate: an unnotified edit fails a test loudly (PASS, `crates/semantic/tests/watch.rs`, on tsrs and the Go checker); Chakra edit-and-query p95 at most 25 ms (PASS at 22.6 ms for a component with props of its own in the Chakra program; FAIL at 565 ms and more for one of Chakra's `ButtonProps`, whose floor is converting its 1,140 props, 330 ms on an unchanged snapshot, while the checker's CPU per edit fell from 437 to 737 ms to 56 to 70: [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#watch-on-snapshotupdate-s6)); 300 Chakra edits stay under the threshold (PASS, peak 321 to 357 MiB against 768, 5 `worn` replacements, answers byte-identical to a fresh session's).
147	7. **S7** Delete the structural resolver for what the suite covers. Gate: every suite row passes with the fallback off on supported platforms; a Windows ARM64 job runs the fallback. (Windows was dropped as a supported platform afterwards, trail 370, so that job no longer exists.) Before any of it goes, the facts the merge took from it come from elsewhere: **S7a** (done) the checker supplies `parent`, `declarations`, tags and `composes` (gate-large: 467,019 of the 467,221 props only the checker returns carry `parent`; the other 202 are members of type literals, which have no parent by definition); **S7a2** (done) oxc's syntax supplies `defaultValue` and union member order, and the checker lane passes with the resolver's answer for them off (`--no-resolver-facts`; [defaults and union order](../type-checker-integration.md#defaults-and-union-order-adr-0026-slice-s7a2)); **S7b** (gate measured) a hidden, test-only `extract --no-structural-fallback` (`ResolverFacts::NoFallback`) merges with no structural fallback, and the checker lane runs every row with it, holding the rows that change in `checker-expectations.json` (`"fallback"`, by cause): 5 of 252, 4 `structural description` (`cross-file/02`, `objects/38`, `objects/39`, `utility-mapped/36`: the checker returns no description the golden has) and 1 `checker could not read: indexedAccess` (`generics/29`), the worklist of S7c to S7e. Fourteen rows (`components`, `cross-file`) cover what only the structural path's own tests held: components made by calls, a `default`-keyed export list, lib-typed functions, a hook's return type, imports, re-exports and shadowed names; all 14 pass on the checker. **S7c** (gate on) the 4 description rows were a missing request: the checker is not asked for a description the structural pass already has (`SemanticTarget::described`, 65% of Mantine's requests), and with no fallback nothing took its place; `ResolverFacts::ready` asks for every description under `NoFallback`, so the default `extract` is unchanged. `generics/29` is a genuine limit: `T["name"]` is an indexed access the checker defers while `T` is open, and PropType has no shape for it, so its answer is the typed `opaque` (`indexedAccess`) with `degradedBy` and a warning. The lane now fails any row that leans on the fallback, listed or not, except a `checker could not read: <kinds>` entry that says in `"limit"` why it is one.
148	8. **S8** (done, 2026-11-12) Make the checker the default (`--no-checker`, `checker: false`), and the docs. The owner flipped it on every surface, `extract` included, knowing the structural speed lead no longer describes the default: `extract` of `gate-large` takes 6.0 s and 970 MiB with the checker against 0.10 s and 200 MiB with `--no-checker` ([gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#the-checker-is-the-default-s8)). The Vite plugin, which has no switch and serves whole outputs, and `watch` stay structural. A session's kept checker answers now share their props, which a session asking every story would otherwise have held at about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component. Gate: `just lint doc-check machete typos` (PASS), and the list below.
149	
150	### Gates before the default flips
151	
152	S8 stays behind these gates (status at the flip, 2026-11-12):
153	
154	- The checker lane of the construct suite (caliper's checker path over `apps/oracle/construct-suite`) shows no regression against the structural path except listed improvements. **PASS**: `just test-checker-lane` on the S8 branch.
155	- Output is deterministic across checker counts on a large program. **PASS in its nearest form** (repeated runs, thread counts, restarts and query order; tsrs's `--api` has no checker count), on the linked checker in trail 369 slice 2 (PR 440).
156	- A Linux CI run of the checker path is green. **PASS**: CI's `Test / Rust` (ubuntu) runs the semantic suite on the built-in checker in every PR.
157	- Memory behaviour past 600 edits in a watch session, with the recycle threshold (768 MiB `max_rss_mib`) exercised. **PASS** in trail 369 slice 2 (PR 440): 650 edits, and the bound crossed stops the linked checker.
158	- The tsrs-against-Go parity check (`pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity`, PR 392) passes on the pinned version, and runs on every pin change. **PASS**: 235 of 235 rows identical on `tsrs` `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, none allow-listed; again on `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the release the product links, in trail 369 slice 4.
159	
160	The determinism and memory gates are measured by `just gate-measure`, on the linked checker since trail 369 slice 2 (both PASS in process); what it reads, and why the first gate's wording cannot be met as written (tsrs's `--api` has no checker-count option), is in [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md). For the linked checker the memory gate's threshold is the same 768 MiB read from its arenas, and crossing it stops the checker rather than recycling it.
161	
162	## Alternatives considered
163	
164	- **Keep the checker opt-in.** Two sources of truth, and the default keeps the silent wrong answers above.
165	- **Checker for the addon only.** The CLI and agents read the same wrong types, and they can afford to wait.
166	- **Spawn the `tsrs` binary** (`@tsrs/<platform>` with the npm packages). Process isolation and a restart lever, but the pipe costs more than the checker (367 against 141 ms on one answer), and every platform needs a binary found or shipped. Rejected; the route that ran one (`--tsc-path`) was deleted in trail 369 slice 4.
167	- **Parse with `tsrs_parser` instead of oxc.** Unpublished like every tsrs crate, and the extractor is written against oxc's AST, which already gives the syntactic facts kept here at about 2 ms per incremental update.
168	- **Keep investing in the structural resolver.** Each defect class above re-implements a checker rule and was silent until a comparison found it.

# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — OXC parses; since 0026 the checker, not a structural pass, decides types on the default path. The first backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- 4. Defer full type-checker integration — removed: superseded by 0006. The gap list and gates are in `docs/type-checker-integration.md`.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()` or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process (it does file I/O but spawns nothing), or route the backend through NAPI.
- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash. Discovery is not yet implemented.
- 8. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs — removed: the invalidation policy of one cache, not a new structure. It lives in `docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md` ("Locked design decisions").
- [9. Write each distinct prop once in the canonical output](0009-canonical-output-interns-props.md) — do not inline props in canonical JSON or derive prop ids from position. Extended by 0018, which groups a component's props into prop sets.
- [10. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer](0010-load-dependency-declarations-by-name.md) — do not load dependency files by import closure, resolve against them lazily during resolution, or emit their components or enums.
