Changing any of these needs a new ADR. A removed entry keeps its number; its rationale moved to the doc named on its line.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A default, threshold or resolution order that one module reads (a collapse limit, a growth count, which lookup goes first) — that's a code comment plus the subsystem's `docs/architecture/` page. Measurements belong in `docs/performance.md`.
- A release or CI procedure (what to publish first, which gate blocks) — that's the workflow file.
- A field added to the canonical JSON under 0017's versioning rule — the `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and `docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md` record it. Write one only when the contract's structure changes, as 0018 did.
- A default flipped after a measurement — the numbers go in `docs/performance.md` and the new default in the option's doc comment.
- A superseded or tuned earlier decision whose design still holds — update the architecture page, don't stack a new ADR on it. Write one only if the contract itself changes.
- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.
# 0026. The checker is the type authority; oxc supplies syntax

**Status:** Accepted (2026-11-08) **Date:** 2026-11-07

## Context

ADR 0006 and 0007 made the TypeScript checker an opt-in second resolver, because a whole-project `tsc` run cost up to 9.3 s and 975 MiB (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`); ADR 0022 bounded it to a warm per-component request. The structural default still answers wrong without a marker: a type that is only a call signature becomes `{}`, `Omit`, `Pick` and `Partial` reached through an alias lose their effect, and a factory's props are taken from a name-matched interface (`docs/rdt-differences.md`, classes 4 to 6). A prototype found more: `[string, ...number[]]` prints as `[string, number[][]]` and a getter reads as a method. Each fix is another rule in a resolver that re-implements the type system.

tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. A throwaway prototype through the Node client (not in the repository; these numbers are the record) measured on Chakra `ButtonProps` (1,138 props) a 43-47 ms snapshot and the first converted prop at 62-67 ms, where ADR 0022 measured 703 ms with `tsc` on a different program root (indicative, not an A/B), with tsrs peaking at 126-130 MiB. On 16 hand-written components the checker was equal or better on 14, worse on union member order and an unresolvable import. A polymorphic component instantiated through a virtual file gave 267 props for `'div'` where both engines give 2 today. tsrs's own benchmark (`bench/RESULTS.md`) reports 1.8 to 4.2 times TypeScript 7.1 beta's speed and 2.1 to 2.6 times less memory.

## Decision

The checker decides types and oxc decides syntax.

- **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.
- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` (`checker: false` in the config, the napi binding and the Storybook addon) turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` are removed (S8).
- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint was re-measured with tsrs in S4 and holds (Chakra's `Button`, 562 ms, 402 ms after the first-answer work). The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).
- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose, never through dependabot (its ignore list); the npm `tsrs` the parity gate runs (`apps/oracle`, `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) moves with them, and `scripts/check-packaging.mjs` fails while the two name different releases. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.
- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed, and there is no other checker to choose. The Go `typescript` beta is the oracle, the construct goldens and the parity gate, in `apps/oracle` only. The linked checker is never replaced, since a fresh session raises this process's memory rather than returning it; past `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, read from its own arenas, it stops for the session and components keep their structural answer with a diagnostic. A panic closes its session and a fresh one answers the next request, and a file nested past 20,000 brackets is not given to it (trail 369 slice 2).
- **React element types.** The checker keeps `ReactElement` and `JSX.Element` as `named` types with their arguments, found by their declaration in `@types/react` (`JSX.Element` named through its namespace, apart from the DOM's `Element`); only `ReactNode` is the `reactNode` terminal. Amended 2026-11-13: this bullet first kept them collapsed to `reactNode`, which is wider (it also admits strings, numbers and `null`) and carried no `degradedBy`, so the construct suite's checker lane scored `react/03` to `05` less precise. The structural fallback still collapses them. No schema change: `named` already holds them.

Linked rather than spawned (trail 369): the crates are published (0.24.0), the same recorded Chakra answer (3,776 requests) takes 141 ms in process against 367 ms over the pipe with equal answers, and there is no per-platform binary to ship or find. What it costs: a stack overflow inside the checker aborts the host process (the 512 MiB thread holds a type 10,000 deep and tsrs's 256 MiB parse threads one 200,000 deep; past 20,000 brackets a file is refused, but nesting written without brackets, such as a chain of 700,000 arrow types, is not bounded), a dropped session does not return its memory (trail 369 slice 2, done: it bounds the checker's arenas and then answers structurally, [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#in-process-guards-trail-369-slice-2)), and each linked artifact grows by about 22 MB.

Trail 369 slice 4 (done, 2026-11-12) deleted the product's process route: `--tsc-path` and `tscPath` (CLI, config, napi, Storybook addon), `crates/tsc-client`, the binary lookup and the version allow-list it checked, and the replay tests that ran recordings of the Go checker through a fake `tsc` process; those tests ask the linked checker now. Slice 5's pin rule is in **Pin** above. Spawning a binary stays rejected (Alternatives).

## Consequences

- Supersedes "structural stays the default" in ADR 0006 and 0007 and 0007's "never a silent default" trigger. The rest of both stands.
- Deletable or shrinkable with a thin fallback, estimated from each file's header: in `crates/core/src/resolver`, `alias`, `chain`, `evaluate`, `substitute`, `named`, `primitives`, `extends`, `func`, `template`, `import`, `callee`, `memo`, `deps`, `collected` and `precedence` shrink to a no-generics subset and `mod.rs` by half; `dependency_types.rs` and `import_map.rs` go (the checker resolves modules; ADR 0010 and 0025 narrow to the fallback); in `extractor`, `interface` (but cva), `alias`, `values`, `reexports`, `asserted` and most of `visit` go, and `component`, `wrapper` and `mod.rs` shrink to candidate detection. About 7,600 of 25,300 non-test lines, 9,400 with no fallback, which Windows ARM64 rules out. `html`, `react`, `ambient`, `evidence`, `uses`, `defaults` and `jsdoc` stay; `crates/semantic` grows and `convert.rs` is rewritten (`crates/tsc-client`, the process route's client, is gone since trail 369 slice 4).
- Contract: `PropType` gains what the checker knows and it cannot hold: tuple element optional, rest and labels, `bigint`, `unique symbol`, enum identity, template literals, overload sets, call signatures on objects, a recursion marker, and a typed truncation in place of `Named` with checker text. React terminals (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `Ref`, `ElementType`, HTML attributes) are recognized by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` (`crates/semantic/src/component.rs`) does. `SCHEMA_VERSION` and `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (ADR 0017).
- No cache is keyed on a type id: ids are per checker and change with query order. Keys are file content, export name, instantiation and the tsrs pin. The checker does not see an edit it is not told about, so watch forwards every change. The whole-project `extract` keeps its answer on disk for the whole program only, keyed by every question its linked checker asked of the file system (failed lookups included) with a digest of each answer, the build's fingerprint (the pin with it) and the request; any different answer discards it whole (2026-11-12, `docs/type-checker-integration.md`).
- Unsolved: a per-component dependency closure from the checker (invalidation stays conservative), and the structural answer's gaps wherever the fallback runs.
- Risks: tsrs is pre-1.0, four releases in twelve days, and closed to pull requests (its README). Memory grew from 98 to 246 MB over 150 Chakra edits with each old snapshot disposed (#920 and #646 open). Determinism across checker counts is shown only on a 72-file program. There is no `@tsrs/win32-arm64` package, so those users get the fallback. The linked crates add about 22 MB to the CLI and to the napi binding.

Migration, each slice behind a deterministic gate, none on the oracle. The tsrs backend (the Rust client running on tsrs, PR 390) is done.

1. **S1** (done) Shared projection model and the new `PropType` variants, filled by the structural path where it knows them. Gate: a unit test per variant, golden JSON diff, cache schema test.
2. **S2** (done) Flag-based converter in `convert.rs`, memoized by type id within one snapshot, with a named-boundary policy and caps. Gate: the construct suite's expected JSON; reversed query order gives identical bytes.
3. **S3** (done) React terminals by declaring path. Gate: no regression against today's Chakra `Button` terminals.
4. **S4** (done, one gate failed) The checker's answer wins when it runs: the addon inside ADR 0022's window, the CLI waiting (`--semantic-timeout-ms`, 10 s), and a prop the checker could not read keeps its structural type with `degradedBy` (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`). Gate: checker-on output equals structural on the suite except a listed set of improvements (held by the checker lane); Chakra first answer at most 150 ms through the Rust client (measured 562 ms, then 402 ms once each answer was parsed once and a type's parts asked for once; FAIL: the floor of that request set with no round trips is about 230 ms, 81% of its bytes the property lists of Chakra's style-prop condition maps, so the seam has to change rather than the budget: [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#first-answer-s4), and ADR 0022's structural-first answer stands); the Storybook harness re-run (not run: it needs the corpora).
5. **S5** (done) Instantiation of generic and polymorphic components through a virtual file: a component whose first type parameter declares a default is read at it, from a file the checker holds in memory (`createSnapshot`'s `fileSystem` layer, read by tsrs and the Go beta alike) in a second snapshot made only when a requested component is generic; an instantiation that does not form keeps the structural props with the checker's error as the reason ([generic components](../type-checker-integration.md#generic-components-adr-0026-slice-s5)). Gate: `Poly<'div'>` gives at least 260 props and `'a'` differs (PASS: 281 and 289, on tsrs and the Go checker, `crates/semantic/tests/instantiate.rs`).
6. **S6** (done, one gate failed) Watch on `snapshot.update` with RSS recycling: the warm checker keeps its snapshot and brings it up to date with `updateSnapshot` (`ensurePrograms`, the files the session announced), and before an answer compares every file its program read with the stamp it had; an unannounced change answers from a fresh snapshot with a warning naming the file ([watch](../type-checker-integration.md#watch-adr-0026-slice-s6)). Gate: an unnotified edit fails a test loudly (PASS, `crates/semantic/tests/watch.rs`, on tsrs and the Go checker); Chakra edit-and-query p95 at most 25 ms (PASS at 22.6 ms for a component with props of its own in the Chakra program; FAIL at 565 ms and more for one of Chakra's `ButtonProps`, whose floor is converting its 1,140 props, 330 ms on an unchanged snapshot, while the checker's CPU per edit fell from 437 to 737 ms to 56 to 70: [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#watch-on-snapshotupdate-s6)); 300 Chakra edits stay under the threshold (PASS, peak 321 to 357 MiB against 768, 5 `worn` replacements, answers byte-identical to a fresh session's).
7. **S7** Delete the structural resolver for what the suite covers. Gate: every suite row passes with the fallback off on supported platforms; a Windows ARM64 job runs the fallback. (Windows was dropped as a supported platform afterwards, trail 370, so that job no longer exists.) Before any of it goes, the facts the merge took from it come from elsewhere: **S7a** (done) the checker supplies `parent`, `declarations`, tags and `composes` (gate-large: 467,019 of the 467,221 props only the checker returns carry `parent`; the other 202 are members of type literals, which have no parent by definition); **S7a2** (done) oxc's syntax supplies `defaultValue` and union member order, and the checker lane passes with the resolver's answer for them off (`--no-resolver-facts`; [defaults and union order](../type-checker-integration.md#defaults-and-union-order-adr-0026-slice-s7a2)); **S7b** (gate measured) a hidden, test-only `extract --no-structural-fallback` (`ResolverFacts::NoFallback`) merges with no structural fallback, and the checker lane runs every row with it, holding the rows that change in `checker-expectations.json` (`"fallback"`, by cause): 5 of 252, 4 `structural description` (`cross-file/02`, `objects/38`, `objects/39`, `utility-mapped/36`: the checker returns no description the golden has) and 1 `checker could not read: indexedAccess` (`generics/29`), the worklist of S7c to S7e. Fourteen rows (`components`, `cross-file`) cover what only the structural path's own tests held: components made by calls, a `default`-keyed export list, lib-typed functions, a hook's return type, imports, re-exports and shadowed names; all 14 pass on the checker. **S7c** (gate on) the 4 description rows were a missing request: the checker is not asked for a description the structural pass already has (`SemanticTarget::described`, 65% of Mantine's requests), and with no fallback nothing took its place; `ResolverFacts::ready` asks for every description under `NoFallback`, so the default `extract` is unchanged. `generics/29` is a genuine limit: `T["name"]` is an indexed access the checker defers while `T` is open, and PropType has no shape for it, so its answer is the typed `opaque` (`indexedAccess`) with `degradedBy` and a warning. The lane now fails any row that leans on the fallback, listed or not, except a `checker could not read: <kinds>` entry that says in `"limit"` why it is one.
8. **S8** (done, 2026-11-12) Make the checker the default (`--no-checker`, `checker: false`), and the docs. The owner flipped it on every surface, `extract` included, knowing the structural speed lead no longer describes the default: `extract` of `gate-large` takes 6.0 s and 970 MiB with the checker against 0.10 s and 200 MiB with `--no-checker` ([gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md#the-checker-is-the-default-s8)). The Vite plugin, which has no switch and serves whole outputs, and `watch` stay structural. A session's kept checker answers now share their props, which a session asking every story would otherwise have held at about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component. Gate: `just lint doc-check machete typos` (PASS), and the list below.

### Gates before the default flips

S8 stays behind these gates (status at the flip, 2026-11-12):

- The checker lane of the construct suite (caliper's checker path over `apps/oracle/construct-suite`) shows no regression against the structural path except listed improvements. **PASS**: `just test-checker-lane` on the S8 branch.
- Output is deterministic across checker counts on a large program. **PASS in its nearest form** (repeated runs, thread counts, restarts and query order; tsrs's `--api` has no checker count), on the linked checker in trail 369 slice 2 (PR 440).
- A Linux CI run of the checker path is green. **PASS**: CI's `Test / Rust` (ubuntu) runs the semantic suite on the built-in checker in every PR.
- Memory behaviour past 600 edits in a watch session, with the recycle threshold (768 MiB `max_rss_mib`) exercised. **PASS** in trail 369 slice 2 (PR 440): 650 edits, and the bound crossed stops the linked checker.
- The tsrs-against-Go parity check (`pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity`, PR 392) passes on the pinned version, and runs on every pin change. **PASS**: 235 of 235 rows identical on `tsrs` `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, none allow-listed; again on `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the release the product links, in trail 369 slice 4.

The determinism and memory gates are measured by `just gate-measure`, on the linked checker since trail 369 slice 2 (both PASS in process); what it reads, and why the first gate's wording cannot be met as written (tsrs's `--api` has no checker-count option), is in [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md). For the linked checker the memory gate's threshold is the same 768 MiB read from its arenas, and crossing it stops the checker rather than recycling it.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the checker opt-in.** Two sources of truth, and the default keeps the silent wrong answers above.
- **Checker for the addon only.** The CLI and agents read the same wrong types, and they can afford to wait.
- **Spawn the `tsrs` binary** (`@tsrs/<platform>` with the npm packages). Process isolation and a restart lever, but the pipe costs more than the checker (367 against 141 ms on one answer), and every platform needs a binary found or shipped. Rejected; the route that ran one (`--tsc-path`) was deleted in trail 369 slice 4.
- **Parse with `tsrs_parser` instead of oxc.** Unpublished like every tsrs crate, and the extractor is written against oxc's AST, which already gives the syntactic facts kept here at about 2 ms per incremental update.
- **Keep investing in the structural resolver.** Each defect class above re-implements a checker rule and was silent until a comparison found it.

# Relevance baseline: do the default outputs show the props consumers pass? (trail 405, track T5)

Read-only measurement. Binary: release build of origin/main 7b8f6d0d (rust 1.99.1), target dir `shrink/target-relevance`. No PR, no push, no oracle run.
Scripts: `shrink/relevance/` (`run-extract.sh`, `run-all.sh`, `callsites.mjs`, `elemprops.mjs`, `gen-elemprops.py`, `analyze.py`). Raw outputs in `shrink/relevance/out/`; the full per-corpus, per-variant numbers (including "outside library src only" and thresholded rules) are in `shrink/relevance/results.md`. Re-run: `run-all.sh`, `run-callsites.sh`, `gen-elemprops.py`, `analyze.py`.

## Method

- Extraction: `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` with defaults (`--collapse-inherited-props dependencies`, `--html-attributes full`), with the checker and with `--no-checker`, on mantine `packages/@mantine/core/src`, react-spectrum `packages`, shadcn-ui `apps/v4`, ant-design `components`. Chakra: `packages/react/src` with `--no-checker` only (never run with the checker). Peak RSS of every run was 0.1 to 1.0 GiB, one process at a time.
- Call sites: TypeScript compiler API walk of every .tsx/.jsx in the whole checkout (skipping node_modules, dist, build). A capitalised JSX tag is resolved syntactically by import/export identity: TS module resolution with the nearest tsconfig (paths), a workspace-package fallback (package.json name to dir/src/index), then re-export chains (`export {a as b} from`, `export *`, `export default X`, local aliases) are followed to a (file, exportName) position. Dotted tags (`Accordion.Item`) are resolved through `X.Item = Y` and `Object.assign(X, {Item: Y})`. The position is matched to caliper's `exports` (file + export name), never by display name. Attribute names only; spreads counted separately and their keys ignored; `key` dropped, `ref` kept.
- `passed` = union of attribute names over the component's call sites; components need >= 3 call sites. `visible` = names in the component's prop sets + `notableInherited` (empty everywhere in these runs). `hidden` = passed, not visible, and in a collapsed inheritance layer. A layer's names are its `members` list when the output has one; otherwise (the layer has `htmlElement` and no member names, which is the case for the `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layers) the names are the props of `JSX.IntrinsicElements["el"]` read from the same @types/react the run loaded (`elemprops.mjs`). That is an assumption: the output itself does not name them (see "What the output lacks"). "Passed but in no list" = neither visible nor in any layer.
- Coverage = |passed ∩ visible| / |passed| per component. Medians are over components.

## Headline numbers, default output (collapsed layers), checker, all call sites

- mantine: 194 components measured. Visible per component median 77, p90 106. Coverage median 1.00, mean 0.86 (53% of components at 100%). Used-but-hidden: mean 0.87 per component, median 0, p90 3, max 13; 169 (component, prop) pairs; 49% strict DOM/ARIA (className, style, id, aria-*, data-*, on*), 84% broad (adds placeholder, value, disabled, role, tabIndex, type, readOnly ...). Top: placeholder 15, id 14, aria-label 12, ref 11, value 11, onClick 9, onChange 9, readOnly 9, disabled 8, role 5, onFocus 4, onKeyDown 4, onMouseLeave 4, tabIndex 4, onMouseDown 3 (components; layers are `React.ComponentProps<input|div|button>`).
- react-spectrum: 255 measured. Visible median 74, p90 113. Coverage median 1.00, mean 0.96 (85% at 100%). Hidden mean 0.05, 98% of components have none; 12 pairs (50% strict, 92% broad): style 3, ref 3, className 3, slot 2, inert 1 (layer `HTMLAttributes<div>`).
- shadcn-ui: 408 measured. Visible median 3, p90 81. Coverage median 0.50, mean 0.43 (27% at 100%). Hidden mean 0.99, median 1, p90 2, max 8; 404 pairs, 76% strict, 95% broad. Top: className 243 components, id 26, aria-label 13, style 12, placeholder 12, type 11, disabled 10, defaultValue 9, onClick 8, htmlFor 8, title 6, ref 6, src 4, alt 4, value 4 (layers `React.ComponentProps<button|div|input|svg>`).
- ant-design: 47 measured. Visible median 17, p90 61. Coverage median 1.00, mean 0.91 (74% at 100%). Hidden mean 0.74, median 0, p90 2, max 8; 35 pairs, 66% strict, 100% broad. Top: className 6, style 6, ref 5, onClick 4, target 2, rel 2 (`React.HTMLAttributes<div>`, `AnchorHTMLAttributes<a>`).

## `--no-checker` output (structural resolver)

The structural resolver does not collapse the HTML attributes here: it lists them, so nothing is hidden and the cost is rows instead.
- mantine: 194 measured, visible median 352.5, p90 389; coverage mean 0.94; hidden 0.
- react-spectrum: 255; visible median 51, p90 123; coverage mean 0.91; hidden mean 0.01 (2 pairs, `ref`).
- shadcn-ui: 408; visible median 281, p90 294; coverage mean 0.94; hidden 0.
- ant-design: 47; visible median 40, p90 305; coverage mean 1.00; hidden 0.
- chakra (`--no-checker` only): 59 measured; visible median 1123, p90 1137; coverage mean 0.97; hidden mean 0.03 (2 pairs, `ref`, layer `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<span>`). 3792 call sites matched among 629 components.
- The residual misses under `--no-checker` are props in no list: mantine 1.75 per component (onClick 13, href 12, target 9, aria-label 9, ref 8: probably props that arrive through Mantine's polymorphic `component`/`renderRoot`; not checked), shadcn `data-slot` 43 and `data-sidebar` 16 (data-* attributes are in no list in either mode), chakra `data-testid`.

## What a rule "show the props consumers pass" would add and cost

- Extra rows = used-but-hidden props per measured component (checker output). Mean: mantine 0.87, spectrum 0.05, shadcn 0.99, antd 0.74. Median 0, 0, 1, 0; p90 3, 0, 2, 2; max 13, 5, 8, 8. Gain: shadcn coverage median 0.50 to 1.00 and mean 0.43 to about 1.0; mantine mean 0.86 to about 0.99 (the rest is the props in no list). Nearly all of the added rows are DOM/ARIA attributes, so the rule is mostly "surface className, id, aria-label, onClick, style, placeholder, type, disabled, value".
- With a frequency floor (props passed at >= max(2, 20% of sites)) the cost drops to mean 0.30 (mantine), 0.03 (spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn), 0.24 (antd) extra rows, p90 1; with a 50% floor 0.26, 0.01, 0.60, 0.12. Shadcn's median coverage stays 0.50 at the 20% floor and reaches 1.00 at 50%, which says the unmet shadcn demand is concentrated in one prop: className accounts for 243 of the 404 hidden-used pairs.
- So the rule is cheap on rows (about 1 row per component, versus 74 to 350 visible rows today) but it needs call-site data the extractor does not have: the signal comes from a consumer corpus, not from the library source. Without that data a static stand-in is the fixed set {className, style, id, aria-*, data-*, ref} plus handlers, which would be the same 1 to 3 rows. Expanding all layers instead costs 280 to 1100 rows per component, as the `--no-checker` numbers show.

## What the output lacks (found while measuring)

- Collapsed layers `React.ComponentProps<"el">` and `HTMLAttributes<el>` carry `htmlElement` and `omitted`, but `members` is empty and `totalProps` is 0 (mantine: all 255 layers; shadcn: 1299 of 1417). A reader of the JSON cannot tell which attributes are inside. Only 106 layers (e.g. `GlobalDOMEvents`) carry a member list. My "hidden" set therefore relies on @types/react; if the layer's real contents differ (for instance `Omit`), the hidden counts move. The "no list at all" figures are the upper bound of what an extractor-side fix would not recover.
- mantine Button (checker and no-checker): 85 props, no inheritance layer, no onClick/href: HTML attributes are in no list at all (`passed but in no list` above).

## Limits, candidly

- Call sites inside the library itself count as consumers in the headline numbers (docs, tests excluded only where the corpus was pruned). `results.md` has the "outside library src only" variant: mantine 176 components, coverage mean 0.88, hidden mean 0.68; react-spectrum only 29 components (corpus is `packages` only, 484 external sites; hidden mean 0.14); ant-design 29, hidden mean 0.72; chakra 55, hidden mean 0.04. For shadcn `apps/v4` is the whole app, so inside and outside cannot be separated (0 sites outside).
- Spread attributes: call sites with at least one spread, averaged over components: mantine 19%, spectrum 34%, shadcn 3%, antd 17%, chakra 5%. Props passed only through spreads are invisible to this oracle, so true coverage demand is understated, most for spectrum.
- Wrappers: a component re-exported through a wrapper that is itself a caliper component (a design-system layer over a primitive) is counted at the wrapper only; what the wrapper forwards is not seen. Unresolved tags: external packages not in the checkout (mantine 769, spectrum 3412, shadcn 3432, antd 474, chakra 1322) and local non-exported bindings (432, 766, 497, 176, 479) are not counted; so spectrum's matched sites are 2761 of 9692 capitalised tags. Dotted members that are not defined by `X.Y = Z` or `Object.assign` are not matched.
- `passed` is a union across call sites (one use is enough), so it overstates demand for rare props; the 20%/50% rows give the frequency-weighted view, and `results.md` also lists call-weighted coverage (median 1.00 everywhere except shadcn 0.50).
- Stories: the checkouts are mostly pruned but two corpora still hold story files. react-spectrum has 132 story files, 25 with `args` (47 distinct keys, e.g. `placeholder`, `onSelectionChange`); chakra has 125 under `__stories__`, only 1 with a `component` meta and `args` (`children`, `variant`). Mantine, shadcn, antd: none. Stories were scanned but not folded into the coverage numbers (too few).
- Chakra: no checker run, as instructed. `checker-default/chakra-only/src` was extracted with and without the checker (688 MiB peak with the checker), but its files are synthetic stubs (`function ChakraAccordionRoot(props: ComponentProps<typeof AccordionRoot>)` importing from `@chakra-ui/react`), so no call site in the Chakra checkout maps to them; it is not included in any figure.
- One snapshot of one commit per corpus, one hidden-set assumption (above), and a syntactic resolver rather than the full checker: an unresolved import silently lowers the component count, never raises coverage.

Scripts: missing.py (per-component missing set), classify.js (TypeScript compiler API, syntax-only, same-file and relative-import resolution), extras.js (typeof import source, heritage text). "Missing" = a prop name the checker lists for a component (own + inherited member sets) and the structural answer does not. Components are matched by key; every component is in both answers (0 checker-only), so no component is lost, only props.

## Summary

- Antd and Mantine: 0 components with missing props. Chakra source corpus: 11 of 629 components, 13 props in total. The structural answer is complete enough there.
- Nearly all the loss is in two real corpora (shadcn 6228 props over 154 components, Spectrum 2216 over 34 components) and in the two synthetic Chakra consumer fixtures (chakra-only: 707 components, 507327 props; gate-large: 770 components, 508163 props; these overlap, do not add them).
- Style-prop sets (bucket counts of components by missing-prop count): chakra-only 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608, 1000+: 0. gate-large 111 / 51 / 608 / 0. shadcn 57 / 97 / 0 / 0. Spectrum 7 / 26 / 1 / 0. Chakra src 11 / 0 / 0 / 0. In the fixtures, 429163 of the missing props are parented to `SystemProperties` and 71500 to `Conditions`, both generated mapped/conditional types inside the installed `@chakra-ui/react` package. The structural answer lists 0 props for those components (e.g. `ChakraComboboxRoot`: 0 vs 899).
- All 706 fixture components declare props as `ComponentProps<typeof X>` where X is imported from the package `@chakra-ui/react` (706 of 706, checked from the import). Declared shape is simple; the content lives in node_modules.
- In shadcn, every missing prop has a node_modules parent (`GlobalDOMEvents` 6171, `HTMLAttributes` 57). Each affected component loses the same roughly 60-63 DOM event handlers (onAnimationEnd, onMouseDown, onPointerMove, ...). Declared shapes are all simple (intersection, Omit, ComponentProps, direct named type); the props come from `react-aria-components`, `cmdk`, `radix-ui` types.
- In Spectrum, 32 of 34 components are wrapped in `createLeafComponent` / `createBranchComponent`, and their props interfaces extend several in-repo interfaces (`Omit<GlobalDOMAttributes<..>,'onClick'>`, `LinkDOMProps`, `PressEvents`, `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>`). The checker lists ~100 props, the structural answer 1 (ListBoxItem 102 vs 1).
- The Chakra source corpus misses only `ref` and recipe variant keys (`inline`, `placement`) on `chakra("div", {...variants})` components.

## Buckets (real corpora = shadcn + Spectrum + Chakra src; 199 components, 8457 missing props)

Primary bucket is the shape of the top-level declared props type (same-file and relative-import resolved), first in the order you listed; the factory/generic/polymorphic/recipe tags only win when the top shape is unresolvable. Overlap counts (components carrying a tag anywhere): shadcn external 70, componentprops 78, wrapper 33, intersection 54, generic 19, unresolved 12; Spectrum factory 32, generic 24, extends 24, componentprops 23, wrapper 17, recipe 10. Fixtures: componentprops 706 of 707. No component had a top-level mapped, conditional, or indexed shape. Polymorphic `as` tagged none that matter. Nothing used `SystemStyleObject` spreads in these components.

- Intersection of named types: 54 components (all shadcn), 2932 props, 34.7%. Examples: AlertDialog (`Omit<ModalOverlayPrimitiveProps,"className"|"children"> & Pick<ComponentProps<typeof ModalPrimitive>,"isDismissable"> & {...}`), missing onAnimationEnd, onAnimationEndCapture, onAnimationIteration, onAnimationIterationCapture, onAnimationStart...; BreadcrumbItem (`BreadcrumbProps & {separatorClassName?}`); TraceCollapsibleTrigger (`Omit<ButtonProps,"className"|"children"|"slot"> & {...}`).
- Interface extends other interfaces: 24 components (all Spectrum), 1874 props, 22.2%. Examples: ListBoxItem (101 missing: onBlur, onFocus, onFocusChange, dir, hidden, inert, lang, suppressHydrationWarning), MenuItem (100), Row (99: render, dir, hidden, inert...).

## Rule-coverability judgement (candid; I did not implement any rule)

- Intersection and Omit/Pick wrapper (shadcn): the declared shape is trivial to parse. A rule would resolve each member, apply Omit/Pick as a key filter and union the members. The blocker is that the member types live in `react-aria-components` d.ts, so a rule needs package/d.ts resolution. Uncovered by inspection: whether those d.ts use only plain interface heritage (then a deterministic walker is enough) or `GlobalDOMAttributes<T>`-style generics over `@types/react`. I only know the parent names, not their definitions. About 100% of these missing props have a node_modules parent. Risk: Omit keys given as unions/aliases, class names mismatched.
- Interface extends (Spectrum): a rule would walk heritage across workspace packages (`@react-types/shared`, `react-aria`) and flatten, applying `Omit<X,'k'>` as a filter. Two of its inputs are not plain: `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>` looks conditional on the tag, and `GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` is generic. Plain heritage (`LinkDOMProps`, `HoverEvents`, `PressEvents`) is rule-coverable given workspace resolution. The structural side listed 1 prop of 102 for ListBoxItem, so heritage across modules is currently not flattened. Likely partial coverage: most of the 100 props come from the plain interfaces and the DOM event set; the conditional alias is the uncertain part.
- `ComponentProps<typeof X>`: if X is local or a workspace/aliased file (shadcn: 9 local, 20 `@/registry/...` aliases), rule = resolve X to its function, take its first param type, recurse. That needs tsconfig `paths`. If X comes from node_modules (`react-aria-components` 28, `cmdk` 21, `radix-ui`, `react-day-picker`; fixtures: `@chakra-ui/react` 706 of 706) the rule needs the d.ts, and for Chakra the 429163 `SystemProperties` + 71500 `Conditions` props come from generated mapped/conditional types. That bucket needs type evaluation unless the owner accepts a fixed lookup table of Chakra's style-prop names (about 845 names per recipe) keyed on the package version. Fragile, and I have no evidence the set is stable across components.
- Other / generic named type from a package: same as above; plus type-argument substitution for `X<T>` (generic default `T = object` is likely irrelevant to prop names, a cheap assumption I did not verify). Namespace imports (`ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`) need namespace resolution.
- Factory (Chakra): `chakra("div", {variants})` is rule-coverable from the call arguments. The 13 missing props are `ref` (added by the factory) and variant keys (`inline`, `placement`), but evidence is 3 components, so the rule is only supported on small samples. Spectrum `createLeafComponent('x', function(props: P, ref, item){})`: coverable by reading the first function parameter, then it falls into the extends bucket. Two Spectrum initializers (as-expression, a nested call) were not unwrapped by my classifier either.
- Highest-value order by missing props: intersection (2932), extends (1874), ComponentProps (1427 + 506621 in the fixtures), other (1050), generic (831). None of the five is rule-coverable without module/package resolution; only the factory bucket (4%) is covered by the call arguments alone. Within real corpora, roughly the Spectrum 22% and the local-alias part of ComponentProps are coverable with workspace resolution; the node_modules-parented shadcn losses (and the Chakra fixtures) need the checker or a bundled type-declaration reader.

- Classification is syntax-only plus resolution through same-file declarations and relative imports; path aliases (`@/...`) and workspace packages are not resolved, which is why several shapes read "external". Top-shape bucket uses that resolution; tags are best-effort.
- Default `--collapse-inherited-props` was used (as asked), not `none`.
- The reverse direction (struct-only props; e.g. Chakra struct lists 1118 props vs checker 845 on Center) was not analysed.
- Missing-prop names for a few examples are limited to the first 5-8 listed above.
- A first accidental build ran with the default toolchain into the worktree `target/` dir (ignored by git) before the proper one; that dir is unused.

# Chakra whole-project extract: 42 GB with the checker on

Date: 2026-11-15. Binary: release-candidate-target/release/caliper-docgen (0.11.0, main 7b8f6d0d). Corpus: corpora/chakra-ui/packages/react/src.

## Summary

- The 42 GB is the Rust heap of the converter's output types (`PropType` trees), not the tsrs checker arenas. mimalloc stats at exit: peak commit 43.5 GiB in mimalloc's own arenas (tsrs arenas are a separate `mmap` range, `tsrs_core-0.24.0/src/reserve.rs:86`), with peak RSS 40.4 GiB, so almost all of it is mimalloc-allocated Rust memory.
- Why it is so large: in this corpus Chakra's style system (`styled-system/`) is *project source*, so `is_own` (crates/semantic/src/convert.rs:339) treats its ~700 `SystemProperties` and its 130 `Conditions` as the project's own members, and `MAX_FIELDS` never cuts own members (convert.rs:1249, "What the project declared itself is never cut"). Every `_hover`, `sm`, `css`, ... prop (type `SystemStyleObject`) expands to about 700 fields × (value union + a 130-field condition object): 24.7 MB of JSON *each*. In the gate fixture (`checker-default/chakra-only`) the same types come from `node_modules`, are a dependency's, and stop at a named boundary, so the gates never saw this.
- The multiplier: `Converter::convert` returns `entry.converted.clone()` on every memo hit (convert.rs:681-686), a deep clone of the tree, and `PropType` has no shared children. The run made 1,729,385 memo hits against 74,401 misses (`type_memo=(1729385, 74401)` in the `-vv` log). Output is 3.87 GB of JSON, and memory is about 10 times that.
- Why the guard missed it: the arena guard (`max_rss_mib`, 768 MiB, `Upkeep::decide`) exists only in `OnDemand` (crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs:491, 646, 656), which serves the Storybook/watch session. `extract` calls the one-shot `resolve_cached_early`/`resolve_early`/`resolve` (crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:187-190, crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:159-208), which has no memory check. Even if it were wired in, it reads only the tsrs arena range with `mincore` (crates/semantic/src/checker.rs:164-171), which leaves out the converter heap where the 40 GB lives. It also checks only between requests, and the first parallel batch of 5 components alone built 39 GB in 5 s.
- Recommended bound (two parts):
  - A size cut in the converter: a converted type larger than a byte or node budget becomes a named `Truncated`. - Count converted nodes or bytes in a shared `AtomicU64` in `State`, incremented on each miss and each memo-hit clone (the size is known from the entry). Alternatively read mimalloc's committed bytes (`mi_process_info`), which also sees the clone.

Also worth doing: `kept::save` should stream to the temporary file (`rmp_serde::encode::write` into a `BufWriter`) instead of building the whole buffer, which was 2.16 GB here.

Risks:
- The size cut changes output only for types over the budget. A project with legitimately large own types (a design-token object) loses their expansion, and a diagnostic must say so.

2	
3	Binary: origin/fix/bound-converted-type-size @ 50cd7dd0 (release, rust 1.99.1, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=shrink/target-census). `git fetch` failed (network denied in the sandbox), so that ref is the local copy and may be stale. Outputs are in shrink/census/. Scripts: missing.py (per-component missing set), classify.js (TypeScript compiler API, syntax-only, same-file and relative-import resolution), extras.js (typeof import source, heritage text). Status: census/status.txt.
4	
5	"Missing" = a prop name the checker lists for a component (own + inherited member sets) and the structural answer does not. Components are matched by key; every component is in both answers (0 checker-only), so no component is lost, only props.
6	
7	## Summary
8	
9	- Antd and Mantine: 0 components with missing props. Chakra source corpus: 11 of 629 components, 13 props in total. The structural answer is complete enough there.
10	- Nearly all the loss is in two real corpora (shadcn 6228 props over 154 components, Spectrum 2216 over 34 components) and in the two synthetic Chakra consumer fixtures (chakra-only: 707 components, 507327 props; gate-large: 770 components, 508163 props; these overlap, do not add them).

In the fixtures, 429163 of the missing props are parented to `SystemProperties` and 71500 to `Conditions`, both generated mapped/conditional types inside the installed `@chakra-ui/react` package. The structural answer lists 0 props for those components (e.g. `ChakraComboboxRoot`: 0 vs 899).

Each affected component loses the same roughly 60-63 DOM event handlers (onAnimationEnd, onMouseDown, onPointerMove, ...). Declared shapes are all simple (intersection, Omit, ComponentProps, direct named type); the props come from `react-aria-components`, `cmdk`, `radix-ui` types.

18	
19	Primary bucket is the shape of the top-level declared props type (same-file and relative-import resolved), first in the order you listed; the factory/generic/polymorphic/recipe tags only win when the top shape is unresolvable. # Which declaration patterns does `--no-checker` miss? (census)

Binary: origin/fix/bound-converted-type-size @ 50cd7dd0 (release, rust 1.99.1, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=shrink/target-census). `git fetch` failed (network denied in the sandbox), so that ref is the local copy and may be stale. Runs were `extract --src <src> --json --quiet --no-cache` with and without `--no-checker`, default `--collapse-inherited-props`, one process at a time under a 14 GB RSS watchdog (1 s sampling). Nothing was killed. Highest checker peak: Chakra 6456 MB; the others were under 900 MB. Short runs under 1 s show peak 0-2 MB, which is the sampling interval and not a real measurement. Outputs are in shrink/census/. Scripts: missing.py (per-component missing set), classify.js (TypeScript compiler API, syntax-only, same-file and relative-import resolution), extras.js (typeof import source, heritage text). Status: census/status.txt.

"Missing" = a prop name the checker lists for a component (own + inherited member sets) and the structural answer does not. Components are matched by key; every component is in both answers (0 checker-only), so no component is lost, only props.

## Summary

- Antd and Mantine: 0 components with missing props. Chakra source corpus: 11 of 629 components, 13 props in total. The structural answer is complete enough there.
- Nearly all the loss is in two real corpora (shadcn 6228 props over 154 components, Spectrum 2216 over 34 components) and in the two synthetic Chakra consumer fixtures (chakra-only: 707 components, 507327 props; gate-large: 770 components, 508163 props; these overlap, do not add them).
- Style-prop sets (bucket counts of components by missing-prop count): chakra-only 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608, 1000+: 0. gate-large 111 / 51 / 608 / 0. shadcn 57 / 97 / 0 / 0. Spectrum 7 / 26 / 1 / 0. Chakra src 11 / 0 / 0 / 0. In the fixtures, 429163 of the missing props are parented to `SystemProperties` and 71500 to `Conditions`, both generated mapped/conditional types inside the installed `@chakra-ui/react` package. The structural answer lists 0 props for those components (e.g. `ChakraComboboxRoot`: 0 vs 899).
- All 706 fixture components declare props as `ComponentProps<typeof X>` where X is imported from the package `@chakra-ui/react` (706 of 706, checked from the import). Declared shape is simple; the content lives in node_modules.
- In shadcn, every missing prop has a node_modules parent (`GlobalDOMEvents` 6171, `HTMLAttributes` 57). Each affected component loses the same roughly 60-63 DOM event handlers (onAnimationEnd, onMouseDown, onPointerMove, ...). Declared shapes are all simple (intersection, Omit, ComponentProps, direct named type); the props come from `react-aria-components`, `cmdk`, `radix-ui` types.
- In Spectrum, 32 of 34 components are wrapped in `createLeafComponent` / `createBranchComponent`, and their props interfaces extend several in-repo interfaces (`Omit<GlobalDOMAttributes<..>,'onClick'>`, `LinkDOMProps`, `PressEvents`, `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>`). The checker lists ~100 props, the structural answer 1 (ListBoxItem 102 vs 1).
- The Chakra source corpus misses only `ref` and recipe variant keys (`inline`, `placement`) on `chakra("div", {...variants})` components.

## Buckets (real corpora = shadcn + Spectrum + Chakra src; 199 components, 8457 missing props)

Primary bucket is the shape of the top-level declared props type (same-file and relative-import resolved), first in the order you listed; the factory/generic/polymorphic/recipe tags only win when the top shape is unresolvable. Overlap counts (components carrying a tag anywhere): shadcn external 70, componentprops 78, wrapper 33, intersection 54, generic 19, unresolved 12; Spectrum factory 32, generic 24, extends 24, componentprops 23, wrapper 17, recipe 10. Fixtures: componentprops 706 of 707. No component had a top-level mapped, conditional, or indexed shape. Polymorphic `as` tagged none that matter. Nothing used `SystemStyleObject` spreads in these components.

- Intersection of named types: 54 components (all shadcn), 2932 props, 34.7%. Examples: AlertDialog (`Omit<ModalOverlayPrimitiveProps,"className"|"children"> & Pick<ComponentProps<typeof ModalPrimitive>,"isDismissable"> & {...}`), missing onAnimationEnd, onAnimationEndCapture, onAnimationIteration, onAnimationIterationCapture, onAnimationStart...; BreadcrumbItem (`BreadcrumbProps & {separatorClassName?}`); TraceCollapsibleTrigger (`Omit<ButtonProps,"className"|"children"|"slot"> & {...}`).
- Interface extends other interfaces: 24 components (all Spectrum), 1874 props, 22.2%. Examples: ListBoxItem (101 missing: onBlur, onFocus, onFocusChange, dir, hidden, inert, lang, suppressHydrationWarning), MenuItem (100), Row (99: render, dir, hidden, inert...).
- `ComponentProps<typeof X>` family: 51 shadcn components, 1427 props, 16.9% (real corpora); plus 706 fixture components, 506621 props. Examples: AlertDialogContent (`React.ComponentProps<typeof AlertDialog>`, 64), ButtonGroupSeparator (`ComponentProps<typeof Separator>`, 64), Textarea (1: `tw`); fixtures ChakraComboboxRoot (899: recipe, allowCustomValue, alwaysSubmitOnEnter, autoFocus...), ChakraSelectRoot (887: recipe, id, 2xl, 2xlDown...).
- Other, a named props type imported from a package (23 `react-aria-components`, 8 unresolved namespace imports such as `ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`): 31 shadcn components plus 2 Spectrum, 1050 props, 12.4%. Examples: Accordion (`DisclosureGroupProps`, 64), AccordionContent (`DisclosurePanelProps`, 64), TableHead (`ColumnProps`, 64); Spectrum `_Card` (12: childItems, hasChildItems, textValue, title; initializer is an `as` expression) and Column (3, declaration not found by name).
- Generic (named external generic, `ListBoxProps<T>`): 15 shadcn components, 831 props, 9.8%. Examples: BreadcrumbList (`BreadcrumbsProps<T>`, 64), ComboboxGroup (`ListBoxSectionProps<T>`, 64), TableRow (`RowProps<T>`, 63).
- Factory/callee call: 11 Chakra + 4 Spectrum components, 335 props, 4.0%. Examples: Chakra Center (`chakra("div",{base,variants})`: inline, ref), InputElement (placement, ref); Spectrum MenuSection (`createBranchComponent`, 85: render, dir, hidden, inert), Divider (81: aria-describedby, aria-details, aria-label, aria-labelledby).
- Plain literal / interface without heritage: 4 Spectrum components, 5 props (Divider `{size?}`, SubmenuTrigger children/delay): the factory wrapper hides them from the structural reader.
- Wrapper (Omit/Pick/Partial) as top shape: 3 shadcn components, 3 props (AlertDialogTitle, DialogTitle, SheetTitle: `tw`).
- Mapped, conditional, indexed, recipe, polymorphic as top shape: 0 components.

## Rule-coverability judgement (candid; I did not implement any rule)

- Intersection and Omit/Pick wrapper (shadcn): the declared shape is trivial to parse. A rule would resolve each member, apply Omit/Pick as a key filter and union the members. The blocker is that the member types live in `react-aria-components` d.ts, so a rule needs package/d.ts resolution. Uncovered by inspection: whether those d.ts use only plain interface heritage (then a deterministic walker is enough) or `GlobalDOMAttributes<T>`-style generics over `@types/react`. I only know the parent names, not their definitions. About 100% of these missing props have a node_modules parent. Risk: Omit keys given as unions/aliases, class names mismatched.
- Interface extends (Spectrum): a rule would walk heritage across workspace packages (`@react-types/shared`, `react-aria`) and flatten, applying `Omit<X,'k'>` as a filter. Two of its inputs are not plain: `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>` looks conditional on the tag, and `GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` is generic. Plain heritage (`LinkDOMProps`, `HoverEvents`, `PressEvents`) is rule-coverable given workspace resolution. The structural side listed 1 prop of 102 for ListBoxItem, so heritage across modules is currently not flattened. Likely partial coverage: most of the 100 props come from the plain interfaces and the DOM event set; the conditional alias is the uncertain part.
- `ComponentProps<typeof X>`: if X is local or a workspace/aliased file (shadcn: 9 local, 20 `@/registry/...` aliases), rule = resolve X to its function, take its first param type, recurse. That needs tsconfig `paths`. If X comes from node_modules (`react-aria-components` 28, `cmdk` 21, `radix-ui`, `react-day-picker`; fixtures: `@chakra-ui/react` 706 of 706) the rule needs the d.ts, and for Chakra the 429163 `SystemProperties` + 71500 `Conditions` props come from generated mapped/conditional types. That bucket needs type evaluation unless the owner accepts a fixed lookup table of Chakra's style-prop names (about 845 names per recipe) keyed on the package version. Fragile, and I have no evidence the set is stable across components.
- Other / generic named type from a package: same as above; plus type-argument substitution for `X<T>` (generic default `T = object` is likely irrelevant to prop names, a cheap assumption I did not verify). Namespace imports (`ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`) need namespace resolution.
- Factory (Chakra): `chakra("div", {variants})` is rule-coverable from the call arguments. The 13 missing props are `ref` (added by the factory) and variant keys (`inline`, `placement`), but evidence is 3 components, so the rule is only supported on small samples. Spectrum `createLeafComponent('x', function(props: P, ref, item){})`: coverable by reading the first function parameter, then it falls into the extends bucket. Two Spectrum initializers (as-expression, a nested call) were not unwrapped by my classifier either.
- Highest-value order by missing props: intersection (2932), extends (1874), ComponentProps (1427 + 506621 in the fixtures), other (1050), generic (831). None of the five is rule-coverable without module/package resolution; only the factory bucket (4%) is covered by the call arguments alone. Within real corpora, roughly the Spectrum 22% and the local-alias part of ComponentProps are coverable with workspace resolution; the node_modules-parented shadcn losses (and the Chakra fixtures) need the checker or a bundled type-declaration reader.

## Caveats

- Classification is syntax-only plus resolution through same-file declarations and relative imports; path aliases (`@/...`) and workspace packages are not resolved, which is why several shapes read "external". Top-shape bucket uses that resolution; tags are best-effort.
- Default `--collapse-inherited-props` was used (as asked), not `none`.
- The reverse direction (struct-only props; e.g. Chakra struct lists 1118 props vs checker 845 on Center) was not analysed.
- Missing-prop names for a few examples are limited to the first 5-8 listed above.
- A first accidental build ran with the default toolchain into the worktree `target/` dir (ignored by git) before the proper one; that dir is unused.

## Appendix: per-corpus counts

- chakra-ui (packages/react/src): 629 checker components, 629 structural, 11 with missing props, 13 missing props. Buckets 1-10: 11. All `factory` (chakra("tag",...)).
- mantine: 348 / 348, 0 missing.
- ant-design (components): 254 / 254, 0 missing.
- react-spectrum (packages): 1415 / 1415, 34 with missing, 2216 props. Buckets 1-10: 7, 11-100: 26, 101-1000: 1. Extends 24 (1874), factory 4 (322), plain 4 (5), other 2 (15).
- shadcn-ui (apps/v4): 1901 / 1901, 154 with missing, 6228 props. Buckets 1-10: 57, 11-100: 97. Intersection 54 (2932), componentprops 51 (1427), other 31 (1035), generic 15 (831), wrapper 3 (3).
- checker-default/chakra-only: 788 / 788, 707 with missing, 507327 props. Buckets 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 706 (506621), intersection 1 (706).
- gate-large: 938 / 938, 770 with missing, 508163 props. Buckets 1-10: 111, 11-100: 51, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 769 (507457), intersection 1 (706).
- Runs: all exit 0. Peak RSS: chakra checker 6456 MB, gate-large 871, antd 886, shadcn 856, spectrum 732, others under 1 GB or unsampled.

Build: origin/main e3350c8c, rust 1.99.1, release caliper-docgen. `extract --json --quiet --no-cache --src <fixture>/src` with the checker (default) and `--no-checker`; `stats` dropped. Scripts: run-extract.sh, diffmap.py, patterns.py, construct.py, report.py in this directory.

## Summary

- chakra-only: 787 components in each run; props answered by both: 8105; equal: 7931 (97.9%); same meaning spelled differently (elementType/ref vs the checker's expansion): 57; structural unresolved or opaque/unexpanded where the checker has a concrete type: 94; structural concrete but different: 23.
  - only in the checker answer: 506621 props; only in the structural answer: 16002 props. Component level: 74 components have identical prop sets and types, 709 differ in which props they list (almost all: structural lists none of a `ComponentProps<typeof X>` or Chakra style-props set), 4 agree on names but have a concretely different type, 0 have an unresolved one.
- gate-large: 938 components in each run; props answered by both: 9735; equal: 9160 (94.1%); same meaning spelled differently (elementType/ref vs the checker's expansion): 137; structural unresolved or opaque/unexpanded where the checker has a concrete type: 355; structural concrete but different: 83.
  - only in the checker answer: 508163 props; only in the structural answer: 32938 props. Component level: 95 components have identical prop sets and types, 835 differ in which props they list (almost all: structural lists none of a `ComponentProps<typeof X>` or Chakra style-props set), 7 agree on names but have a concretely different type, 1 have an unresolved one.
- Headline, both fixtures pooled: of 17840 props both lanes answer, a shrink that marks type-level cases pending would change 555 (3.11%): 106 concrete wrong types (the flash) plus 449 unresolved/unexpanded ones. 17091 (95.8%) structural concrete answers are right today and must stay; 194 more are right in meaning and need a normalization, not a pending mark.
- The bigger gap is not per-prop type error but missing props: 1014784 props exist only in the checker answer (mostly Chakra style props, `_hover`-style pseudo props and conditions) against 48940 only in the structural one (inherited HTML attributes the checker does not list for those components). A shrink that marks a component pending when its props come from `ComponentProps<typeof X>`, intersections or generic factories removes most of this.
- Construct suite (252 rows): the structural lane is not green on 35 rows (27 less precise, 7 opaque with marker, 1 missing, none wrong); the checker lane is green on all but 4 rows, where the golden itself is cut at the depth limit (not judged). The checker lane reads green on 34 of the 35 structural gaps; the 35th (react/16-ref) is one of the 4 depth-cut rows. See the construct section for the families.

## Reading the classes

- Equal compares the canonical type JSON after sorting union members and reading `literalUnion` as a union of string literals.
- Unresolved means the structural top-level is `opaque`, `truncated`, `unknown`, `any` or an unexpanded `named` alias, or holds an `opaque` node the checker does not. This overlaps with what a pending mark would already cover; it is the safe class.
- Props are compared by name within a component, own and inherited together (a prop set and the `inheritance` members).

## Notes on the concrete-different class

- 60 of the 106 props are function props whose shape matches but a parameter type is a nested alias the structural side leaves named while the checker expands it (for example `DateValue` against `CalendarDate | CalendarDateTime | ZonedDateTime` in Chakra's date-picker `format`, `parse`, `createCalendar`, `isDateUnavailable`). The kind is right and the top-level is right; only the nested detail differs. These are the cheapest wrong-type flashes to hide, and they come from generic aliases and unions written through an alias in a parameter.
- 12 are `React.ReactElement` read as `reactNode` (wider). The same cause shows in the construct suite (react/03, 04, 05, 35, 36, 37).
- 14 are `Partial<XClasses>` kept as a `Partial` application beside the checker's expanded object (MUI `classes`).
- The rest are one-offs: type parameters (`ChakraShow.when`, `ChakraFor.each`: `T` read as `unknown`), `Breakpoint | false`, `TableCellBaseProps['scope']` (an intersection of two strings against `string`), and slot-prop objects with a nested difference.
- Cause labels come from the declared source text found by a regex in the declaring file (the interface named in `parent`, then the first `name?:` line), so a label is a best reading, not a parse. Two categories asked for have no concrete-different instance in these fixtures: conditional types and template literals appear only in the unresolved class (MUI `OverridableStringUnion<...>` with a template literal, Chakra `ConditionalValue<...>`), and call returns do not appear in either fixture (`ReturnType`, `Parameters` appear in the construct suite only).

## Construct suite (apps/oracle/construct-suite, 252 rows)

Source: the committed `expectations.json` (structural lane against the Go-checker goldens, `--no-checker`) and `checker-expectations.json` (checker lane), read by construct.py. I did not re-run the suite: it needs pnpm and the oracle harness, and those files are the gate CI holds. The goldens are the `typescript-beta` (Go) checker captures. No row is `wrong`.

- Structural lane differs from the Go golden on 35 rows: 27 `less precise`, 7 `opaque with marker`, 1 `missing`. 217 rows are identical or spelled.
- Checker lane differs from the Go golden on 4 rows, all `not judged` (the golden's own type is cut at the normalizer's depth limit: generics/19-recursive-json, react/16-ref, react/27-sx-object, react/30-dispatch-setstate). No checker row is wrong or less precise. 34 of the 35 structural gaps read green in the checker lane; the 35th is react/16-ref, which is `not judged` there.
- Structural against checker by category directory:
  - utility-mapped: 12 of 36 rows differ. `ReturnType`, `Parameters`, `Awaited`, `typeof value`, conditional with `infer`, and an alias chain stay unevaluated applications or named references (unresolved, 7 less precise rows); `keyof`, `keyof typeof`, `Base[keyof Base]`, `Empty[keyof Empty]`, `Parameters<H>[0]` are opaque with a marker (5 rows). All are type-level evaluation the structural path cannot do; none is a concrete wrong answer.
  - react: 13 of 37 rows differ. Concrete but wrong or lossy: `ReactElement`, `ReactElement<...>`, `JSX.Element` read as the wider `reactNode` (react/03, 04, 05, 35, 36, 37, six rows) and `PropsWithChildren<{...}>` missing `children` (react/33). ## What
